g_policy.reason: The offer copy states the reward ($1 to PayPal), the player opts in by tapping the button, declining leaves the pop-up unchanged, and 'if the ad fails' hides the button or sends no money.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is '1 US dollars paid to the player's PayPal', which is cash paid out of the app.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is tapping Play at 0 lives, which is an app event, and no chat content is used.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal says 'removes nothing free: yes' and it only adds a button; lives and the timer are unchanged.

g_brand_safety.reason: The offer is a button in the out-of-lives modal (s02), which sits over the level map and is rated safe; this is not a chat screen.

c1_revealed_value.reason: The reward is money, not the resource the app limits (lives). An existing_anchor fails if the app neither charges for nor limits the resource the reward gives, and the app does not charge or limit PayPal dollars.

c2_evidence.reason: The claims about 5 lives, the 30-minute regeneration, and gold bars bought with real money match m01, m02, s02.e02 and s02.e03. The new sponsored-game screen and PayPal note are proposal additions.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: No subscription exists, and the reward does not give lasting access to anything the app charges for or take anything from other users.

c5_moment.reason: The offer appears in the out-of-lives modal right after the player hits the limit, which is a moment of need.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The reward is granted after a play-to-earn game, and the trigger (tapping Play at 0 lives) is a detectable app event. The proposal says 'If the game doesn't count, no money is sent'.

c7_specific.reason: It names the out-of-lives pop-up (s02), the gold-bar button, and the 5-lives/30-minute mechanic of this app.

other_concern: Paying $1 per play, up to 3 times a day, could cost more than the ad earns. It also undercuts the gold-bar sale, since a player can get cash instead of buying lives, despite the rationale's claim otherwise. Also, the reward does not give lives, so it does not relieve the out-of-lives state.
